2.  26-54608  Recommendation to receive and file a presentation on the FY 2025 Continuum of
  Care (CoC) Program Performance Evaluation Results.

  A motion was made by Member McFadzen, seconded by Member
  Rockenbach, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the
  following vote:

  Yes:  10 Amick, Boyce, Brown-Shock, Diles III, McFadzen, Rockenbach,
  Topolewski, Scott, Shuford, Wee
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 3 Lock, Martins, Tan

  • Health Department staff Joseph Botelho provided an overview on updates
  regarding the 2025 CoC program performance evaluation results and review
  data analysis for select metrics.
  • HUD requires CoCs to review, assess and score project applications.
  • Scores factor in the current and past two reporting periods to acknowledge
  historical strong performance and to consider smaller project size. CoC
  Board approves project scores through approval of Priority Listing.
  • Performance scores are used to rank all projects for funding consideration,
  scores are also used to determine reallocation for rants demonstrating poor
  performance.
  • The Long Beach CoC Portfolio includes 23 projects totaling $11,925.969.
  • Metric points are earned by passing a threshold not evenly distributed based
  on scores.
  • Transitional housing projects have the largest range between lowest
  performing and highest performing.
  • A metric review on project performance and fiscal performance was
  discussed using the charts provided in the presentation.
  • Projects score pretty low on Neutrality, these outcomes are measured across
  all Long Beach programs.
  • No priority list was submitted ti HUD this time around.
  • The reallocation policy was applied and the chart provided was discussed,
  projects can be exempt for a variety of reasons.
  • HUD will be asking to measure projects on supportive service participation
  requirements in the future and will be scoring CoCs as well on that.
  • Staff want to narrow some metrics to better align with HUD in order to
  be compliant.
  • Staff want to recommend a sliding scale, the purpose of this would be to

3.  26-54609  Recommendation to review and discuss proposed updates to the Long Beach
  Continuum of Care (CoC) Governance Charter and Bylaws.

  A motion was made by Member McFadzen, seconded by Member
  Rockenbach, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the
  following vote:

  Yes:  11 Amick, Boyce, Brown-Shock, Diles III, Lock, McFadzen, Rockenbach,
  Topolewski, Scott, Shuford, Wee
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 2 Martins, Tan

  • Health Department staff Joseph Botelho provided a brief overview on the
  proposed updated changes to the Charter and Bylaws last updated and
  approved April 2025.
  • The purpose of these updates is to align with HUD requirements, clarify roles
  and responsibilities, formalize the general membership and formalize the
  City of Long Beach’s role as administrative and operational lead.
  • Amendments include expanding approval authority for the CoC Board to
  update Governance Charter and Bylaws is delegated by the CoC General
  Membership. Mandate open public comment period piror to the Board
  Approval.
  • A revision was made to the standing subcommittees, language was revised
  not to mandate appointment from General Membership.
  • Placeholder language was included for the ABLE board until they are able to
  reconvene.
  • Looking further ahead the Long Beach Coc Governance Charter Ad Hoc will
  meet on the 27th after public comment closes to review any feedback and
  finalize revisions to present to the Board.
  • Member Rockenbach had a question regarding pg.4 regional coordination.
  Staff member responded.
  • A member of the public recently shared concerns about housing justice for
  individuals experiencing homelessness and expressed interest in connecting
  with staff working on efforts to support the unhoused community in Long
  Beach.

4.  26-54610  Recommendation to conduct and approve the election of one dedicated and two
  at-large Continuum of Care Board Members pursuant to the Continuum of Care
  Governance Charter.

  A motion was made by Member McFadzen, seconded by Member Shuford, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  11 Amick, Boyce, Brown-Shock, Diles III, Lock, McFadzen, Rockenbach,
  Topolewski, Scott, Shuford, Wee
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 2 Martins, Tan

  • Health Department staff Joseph Botelho provided a brief
  overview of eligibility requirements for the Long Beach Continuum of Care
  (CoC) board members. A total of five (5) applications were received.
  • Applicants present were given the opportunity to provide a two-minute
  summary of their background and their interest in joining the Board.
  • The board will vote on one (1) open seat designated for the Long Beach
  CoC/ESG subrecipient and two (2) at-Large seats representing General
  Membership affiliations.
  • For the record the first vote was to appoint Jacob Munoz to the Long Beach
  CoC/ESG subrecipient seat. A roll call vote was conducted, and the motion
  passed with eleven (11) affirmative votes.
  • A second roll call vote was conducted to appoint one at-Large
  seat representing General Membership affiliations. Applicant Valerie
  Williams was appointed with eleven (11) affirmative votes.
  • A third roll call vote conducted to appoint one at-Large seat representing
  General Membership affiliations. Applicant Travion Chamberlin was
  appointed with seven (7) affirmative votes.
  • No public comment.

5.  26-54611  Recommendation to receive and file a presentation on California Advancing and
  Innovating Medi-Cal (CalAIM).

  A motion was made by Member McFadzen, seconded by Member Brown-
  Shock, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

  Yes:  11 Amick, Boyce, Brown-Shock, Diles III, Lock, McFadzen, Rockenbach,
  Topolewski, Scott, Shuford, Wee

  • Health Department staff Hanna Sampson provided an overview on California
  Advancing and Innovating Medi-Cal (CalAIM), there are programs under this
  new initiative, enhanced care management, community supports, behavorial
  health payment reform and population health management.
  • CalAIM funded approximately 50/50 with Federal and State government
  funds, largely funded by Medicaid 1115 waiver which is currently set to run
  through end of 2026.
  • The state has restructured Community Supports and Enhanced Care
  Management as a Medi-Cal benefit deeming the Medicaid waiver
  unnecessary for continued funding.
  • ECM and Community Supports work in tandem together, ECM can be
  thought of as the coordinator and Community Supports are the resources.
  • The Homeless Services Bureau is contracted to provide Housing deposits,
  Housing Tenancy and Sustaining Services, Housing Transition, Navigation
  Services, and Day Habilitation Services.
  • A list of services that staff provide to the client from the start of their
  connection until the end of service was discussed. The client can be with us
  for up to 3 years.
  • The CalAIM team currently consists of three members and is expected to
  expand in the near future.
  • Members of the board ask questions regarding the expansion to add
  additional providers, where is the funding to for this coming from, where is
  the housing for these clients going to be located and what does the provider
  network look like in the City of Long Beach?
  • Members share concerns regarding our unhoused community and the lack of
  housing

  Yes:  10 Amick, Boyce, Brown-Shock, Diles III, McFadzen, Rockenbach,
  Topolewski, Scott, Shuford, Wee

  • Health Department staff Joseph Botelho provided an overview, the 2025
  NOFO remains enjoined. Staff are waiting on updates for CoC projects, if
  awards are not made my July 1st appropriations language says that HUD
  should provide that non competitive renewal by July 1st . HUD is expected to
  issue the 26 NOFO no later than June 1st to make awards no later than
  December 1st.
  • HUD requires CoCs have coordinated, inclusive outcome oriented
  community process to solicit, review, rank and select project applications to
  submit to HUD. The purpose of the policies is to adhere to the competition
  requirements.
  • The Ad Hoc Committee would consist of 3 to 6 board members that would
  meet virtually between now and the end of the competition. Communities are
  starting their competition review and that is why staff are recommending
  these committees now.
  • The three committees with list of recommended members was discussed
  between members and staff.
  • No public comment.
